name: Astera Labs
thesis: Connectivity silicon (retimers, Scorpio switches) inside AI racks; Q2 revenue $392M, +104% YoY. $354.85 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-0.8%), giving back a little after the 42% run from the Sep 15 low of $251.97; Zacks made it Bull of the Day and Fubon has a $500 target. Scorpio X becoming the largest product line in Q3 is the proof point.
risks: ~175x earnings and within 10% of the $390 consensus target, so the easy rebound is done. Few hyperscaler customers, and Nvidia NVLink competes directly.

name: Broadcom
thesis: Top custom AI chip (XPU) and AI networking supplier; Q3 FY26 AI revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY, Q4 guide ~$34.8B total revenue. $354.46 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-0.2%), still roughly flat since Sep 14 while peers ran; ARK bought 76.2K shares Monday. Consensus target $532 (+50%) is the widest gap among the AI names.
risks: Off-balance-sheet guarantees on Anthropic chip financing ($35B done, ~$60B more discussed). China's SASAC is surveying Broadcom switches in state data centres ahead of possible guidance to cut use.
catalyst: Q4 FY2026 earnings ~2026-12-10 (est.); any SASAC guidance on switches

name: SK hynix
thesis: Holds ~58% of HBM revenue share; Q2 operating income KRW 60.5T at a 76% margin, and the stock trades near 9x earnings. Seoul closed Wednesday at KRW 1,776,000 (+0.6%) and the ADR is $186.12 at 10:30 ET (-0.3%), flat into Micron's print after the bell (consensus revenue $51.5B, +355%; EPS $31.83). Micron's guide sets the tone for HBM pricing into 2027; the Solidigm IPO (up to $100B, 2027) is the overhang.
risks: A separate Solidigm listing adds an ownership layer investors already discount. Memory is the most volatile part of any AI selloff, Bernstein cut its target to 2.7m won on slower HBM4 pricing, and CXMT is closing the gap.
catalyst: Micron results after the bell Wed Sep 30 (Thu 06:30 AEST); Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-10-27 (est.); Solidigm IPO bank selection

name: Bloom Energy
thesis: On-site fuel cells for AI data centres; Q2 revenue $1.07B, +166%, 2026 guide $3.9-4.2B. $286.59 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-1.6%) after Tuesday's 10.8% jump on the Fremont expansion that nearly doubles production space; RBC $335 and Morgan Stanley $310, but Jefferies sits at $264 flagging execution risk. Still +230% YTD.
risks: Trades at the $286 consensus target at ~380x earnings, and swings of 8-11% a day in both directions are now normal. Oracle's Jupiter force majeure stands: gas pipeline slipped to Feb 2027, fuel-cell air permit due Nov 23. Several class actions pending.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings 2026-10-27; Jupiter air-quality permit decision by 2026-11-23

name: GE Vernova
thesis: Bottleneck supplier of gas turbines and grid gear for AI power; Q2 orders $24.2B (+88% organic), backlog ~$176B. $952.30 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-1.1%) after Tuesday's NRC construction permit for TVA's BWRX-300 at Clinch River, the first US SMR permit; declared a $0.50 quarterly dividend Wednesday (record Oct 27, paid Nov 24). Consensus target ~$1,172-1,237 (+23-30%).
risks: Premium multiple on a cyclical business (GLJ Sell, $470 target). Tariffs cost $100-200M in 2026, offshore wind still loses money, and TVA has no construction date or cost-sharing deal yet for the SMR.

name: Vertiv Holdings
thesis: Power, thermal and liquid-cooling infrastructure for AI data centres; Q2 net sales $3.27B (+24%, 18% organic) at a 22.6% adjusted operating margin, with 2026 guidance of $14.0B and 31% organic growth. $243.25 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-2.0%), the weakest of the AI-power names today on no company news; Wells Fargo Overweight at $340, BofA US 1 list, and a Slovakia cooling-plant expansion announced Tuesday. Consensus $338 (+39%).
risks: 56x earnings prices in the guide; Q2 organic growth was 18% with acquisitions and FX doing the rest, so the second half has to accelerate. Hyperscaler capex concentration, and Schneider, Eaton and Asian OEMs compete in liquid cooling. Added at medium conviction until Q3 confirms the ramp.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-10-22 (est.); KES deal close Q4

name: Robinhood Markets
thesis: Q2 revenue $1.31B (+32%) at a 57% adjusted EBITDA margin. Summit follow-through: Robinhood Agents (OpenAI and Anthropic models, ~150K agentic accounts already open since May, trade-by-trade approval on by default, one OpenAI model free to year-end) roll out over coming weeks, plus crypto perps, earnings contracts with Cboe and weekend equities in 2027. Stock rose 2% premarket then faded to $114.41 at 10:30 ET (-1.6%): a sell-the-news day. Deutsche Bank trimmed to $134 (Buy), KBW to $115, BTIG $135; consensus $133 (+16%).
risks: Perps and autonomous AI agents draw regulators; two engineers were charged Sep 15 with insider trading on crypto listings. Revenue swings with retail and crypto volumes at ~50x earnings, and Robinhood bills for model usage it has not disclosed the economics of.
catalyst: Robinhood Agents rollout in October; Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-11-04 (est.)

name: MercadoLibre
thesis: LatAm's leading e-commerce and fintech platform; Q2 revenue $10.17B (+50%), the 30th straight quarter above 30%. $1,711.25 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-0.8%), down 2.4% since Sep 28 and 11% since Sep 14 on no company news; consensus target $2,272 (+33%).
risks: Operating margin is 6.7%, down from 12.2%, as it spends on shipping, credit and one-hour Sao Paulo delivery. Nu is competing hard in lending.

name: Cloudflare
thesis: Edge network that controls bot and AI-agent traffic; Q2 revenue $696M (+36%), 120% net retention. $348.82 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-1.0%), 3% under the Sep 22 record. Deutsche Telekom's T-Systems now resells Cloudflare security across Europe with direct interconnection, and the public post-quantum certificate authority launches Q1 2027.
risks: Trades above the $337 consensus target at ~47x sales, so any growth miss will be punished. Gross margin fell 320bps to 73.1%.

name: Sea Limited
thesis: Q2 revenue $7.8B (+48%): Shopee GMV +28%, Monee loan book $11.1B at 1.0% NPLs. $97.60 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-1.0%), down 10% since Sep 14 on no company news; Monee added a Great Eastern insurance tie-up for Shopee buyers. Consensus target $157 (+61%), still the widest gap on the list.
risks: Competition from TikTok Shop and Temu, and the Brazil push opens a second front against MELI. A Shopee executive's entity sold 60K shares Sep 21-22 under a 10b5-1 plan; the drift lower has no catalyst to stop it before Nov 10.

name: BYD
thesis: Exports drive growth: August overseas sales +134.5% YoY and European sales more than doubled, with local truck production in Europe planned. Closed HK$75.60 Wednesday (-0.2%), sitting on the 52-week low into Thursday's September sales release; a 16 GWh battery plant started up and BYD expects the Formula S series to reach 15,000 units a month. Consensus HK$125.70 (+66%). USD at 7.8457 HKD (Yahoo, 30 Sep).
risks: August China sales -14.3% as Geely, Xpeng and Leapmotor take share; the price war squeezes margins and EU tariffs hang over exports. The tape says nobody wants it ahead of the September number, so a weak print can push it through the low.
catalyst: September sales 2026-10-01; Da Han launch 2026-10-13; Q3 2026 results 2026-10-29

name: Keyence Corp
thesis: Machine vision and sensors for factory automation and robotics; fiscal Q1 sales +33%, net income +51%, operating margin above 50%. Closed JPY 80,480 Wednesday (+1.3%, +5% since Sep 15) at USD/JPY 156.95, a second straight up day with no company news; Citi JPY 95,000, consensus JPY 97,867 (+22%).
risks: The premium multiple assumes 30%+ growth. A stronger yen or slower China capex would hit both earnings and the multiple; Toyota's August numbers show Chinese and US auto demand softening.

name: ASML Holding
thesis: Sole EUV supplier; 2026 guide EUR 43-45B at 54-56% gross margin, 2027 EUV capacity essentially sold out. $1,818.18 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-0.9%) after Tuesday's 3.6% jump on the semi rotation; still +16% since Sep 14. Consensus $2,116 (+16%).
risks: China export limits and proposed US chip tariffs. Sentiment-driven days cut both ways (-7.3% on Sep 14), and the Oct 14 bookings number has to back the rally.

name: Teradyne
thesis: Test equipment for AI and HBM chips (~70% of revenue) plus Universal Robots cobots; Q2 revenue $1.33B, more than double. $396.06 at 10:30 ET Wednesday (-1.7%), giving back some of the 23% run since Sep 14 ahead of Micron; Magnum E2 memory tester (LPDDR6, DDR6, GDDR7, NAND) shows at SEMICON West Oct 13-15. Consensus $446 (+13%).
risks: The most volatile AI name on the list (-13.3% on Sep 14) at a premium multiple, and it trades as a Micron derivative into tonight's print. Test orders are lumpy and come from a few customers.
catalyst: Micron results after the bell Sep 30; Q3 2026 earnings 2026-10-27

name: Tesla
thesis: Car demand is falling while the valuation rests on robotaxi, storage and Optimus. It lined up $30B of new credit (a $20B delayed-draw term loan plus $8B five-year and $2B one-year lines, Citi and Wells Fargo agents) to back capex of more than $25B this year, saying it won't draw in 2026; the SEC also cleared a program letting retail holders auto-vote with the board at every meeting. $351.20 at 10:30 ET (-0.5%). Track it, don't chase it.
risks: Free cash flow is thin at $25B+ capex, which is why the credit lines exist. The auto-vote program is a one-way switch that smooths any SpaceX merger vote and Musk's change-of-control pay; JPMorgan cut to $415 and trimmed Q3 deliveries; EU-wide FSD vote is December at the earliest.
catalyst: Q3 deliveries 2026-10-02; Roadster demo 2026-10-15; Q3 earnings 2026-10-28
